document_summary: New Jersey P.L. 2026, c.43, the Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act, approved July 20, 2026, which bars algorithmic rent-setting coordination and amends the state Antitrust Act framework for residential rentals statewide.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Makes it unlawful, and a violation of the NJ Antitrust Act, for rental property owners to pay for or use a coordinator's services, for coordinators to facilitate rent-restricting agreements, and for anyone to perform a coordinating function or engage in parallel pricing coordination.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting coordination (use of coordinators / algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners (anyone owning one or more rental residential dwelling units) and coordinators operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function. Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
rules.exemptions: Excludes spreadsheets operating without AI and requiring human analysis, and databases that only query unprocessed data. Also excludes research/statistical/testing use of information not used to set rents, free public rent estimates, equal-terms real estate brokerage databases that do not set or recommend rents, and government affordability controls.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) prohibits municipalities from enacting ordinances that conflict with this act, except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law. This may preempt local algorithmic-rent ordinances such as those of Jersey City and Hoboken once effective. The act is in addition to the NJ Antitrust Act.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a. a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator; b. a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function;
rules.conflict_note: Possible preemption of the Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic-rent ordinances: section 6(b) bars municipal ordinances that conflict with the act. This document does not name those ordinances or resolve whether they conflict.
rules.extraction_notes: Section 9: takes effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following enactment. Enacted (approved) July 20, 2026, so the twelfth month following is July 2027, giving 2027-07-01. Not yet effective as of the 2026-10-01 query date. Text is the first reprint (A3497 1R ACS).
